subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should per-job elevated cron and heartbeat authority be implemented as a narrow OpenClaw core feature now, or folded into the broader Gateway-owned scheduling provenance design from #71712?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the durable trust boundary affects elevated exec, cron persistence, heartbeat autonomy, auditability, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the authority model alone.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Use #71712 as the broader design vehicle while explicitly requiring per-job elevated authority and heartbeat provenance in that design.

options.title: Ship Narrow Core Provenance First
options.body: Implement a smaller stored approval/provenance contract for cron and heartbeat elevated execution before the broader playbook/quota API lands.

options.title: Keep Provider Allowlists Only
options.body: Accept the current provider/sender allowlist model and close this as not planned, leaving heartbeat and cron elevation governed by existing config.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Use #71712 as the broader design vehicle while explicitly requiring per-job elevated authority and heartbeat provenance in that design.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently landed the adjacent cron caller-scope boundary and can route the remaining elevated-exec provenance work to the right cron/Gateway/security owners.
